title: Why serious AI builders are skipping third-party evals
excerpt: In-house AI evaluation is the new competitive differentiator
content_html:
As AI copilots, autonomous agents, and conversational companions continue their march into the mainstream, the teams tasked with evaluating them are no longer asking: Did the model produce the correct answer?

Increasingly, they are asking whether the system was engaging enough and created enough value for users to return tomorrow, next week or next month.

It is a shift that fundamentally changes what evaluation means.

Co-Founder and COO, Kaon AI.

In the age of AI, "good" is a moving target. What delights one user may frustrate another, and what offers value to one business could be deemed irrelevant by the next.

That’s why success can no longer be measured solely through generic, external benchmarks, telemetry dashboards, or "LLM-as-a-judge" scores.

Real-time signals

Models grow stronger today not by adhering to an external standard, but based on traces and real-time signals from inside the organization. Evaluation, in fact, is becoming a core part of how organizations build and protect their competitive advantage.

Companies are increasingly creating private evaluation systems in-house that measure progress against outcomes that matter to their business, using real workflows, institutional knowledge, and accumulated judgment as the standard.

The new goal is not simply to assess model performance, but to create a learning loop where human expertise continuously improves AI systems and AI systems amplify human expertise in return.

This feedback cycle turns organizational knowledge into a compounding asset. Every interaction generates new training signals, strengthens institutional memory and improves future performance.

In this new world, private evaluation is the mechanism through which firms build, retain and compound their unique intellectual capital.

Tools no longer fit for purpose

In agentic systems, the quality of the experience emerges over long sequences of interactions rather than individual outputs.

Many evaluation benchmarks still rely heavily on turn-level analysis, measuring isolated prompt-response pairs against predefined criteria. Those can identify a model's capabilities in theories – hallucinations, toxicity or syntax errors – but they can’t reliably determine whether a forgotten preference, a broken memory chain or a subtle degradation in user experience caused a user to disengage days or weeks later.

With the growing adoption of consumer AI, preference learning increasingly operates across the entire user journey instead of within isolated prompts. A dashboard can score an individual response, but it cannot fully understand why a user returned three days later, abandoned a workflow midway through a session or learned to fully trust one interaction versus another.

Those signals often live inside the product itself.

AI redefining evaluation: first-party takes the stage

This is why evaluation is moving from a support function on the sidelines to a core product capability.

Development teams are increasingly moving away from external dashboards and generalized scoring systems and building proprietary feedback loops directly into their products. These systems combine behavioral analytics, user retention data, preference learning, reinforcement signals and post-training pipelines tailored to their own applications.

Their reasoning is simple: staying close to the user is the only way to understand what "good" actually means.

The AI companies poised to win are those building closed-loop systems that connect user behavior, offline analysis, reward-model recalibration and online validation. The most advanced AI products already use live behavioral feedback to refine responses, personalize interactions and improve retention.

Static offline benchmarks are giving way to live preference learning. Isolated, single-turn tests are being replaced by trajectory-level behavioral analysis. Evaluation is moving from the support layer to the core operating system of AI products.

The fate of traditional eval vendors

So where does this leave well-known platforms such as LangSmith, Arize, and Weights & Biases as AI providers absorb more of the stack?

Interestingly, the biggest threat these companies face may not come from Anthropic or OpenAI, but from their own customers.

These vendors are not necessarily being displaced from above. They are increasingly being bypassed and disregarded from below as AI companies realize that evaluation is inseparable from the product itself.

Generic third-party platforms can determine whether an answer resembles benchmark data. External observability vendors can process telemetry and surface analytics. But they are not truly connected to the context that increasingly defines product quality.

Every serious AI company is now discovering the same thing: evaluation is the product. And companies cannot outsource their product.

Defining success is the new critical moat

This shift is accelerating because the rest of the AI stack is becoming increasingly commoditized.

Access to high-performing foundation models is rapidly expanding. Startups and enterprises alike can access powerful APIs with relatively low barriers to entry. Prompt engineering is unlikely to remain a durable differentiator. Basic orchestration layers are becoming standardized. Even generic "LLM-as-a-judge" scoring systems are increasingly available as built-in platform features.

As those layers become commodities, a company's internal understanding of user success becomes a more important differentiator.

The signals that matter for a coding assistant differ from those that matter for a healthcare agent, a tutoring system or an AI companion. Even within the same category, companies may optimize for entirely different outcomes, including engagement, trust, efficiency, emotional resonance or long-term retention.

In a world where models, infrastructure and tooling are increasingly rented, defining success is something that can and must be owned. In fact, it may become the most important piece of intellectual property a company owns.

content_html_zh:
随着人工智能副驾驶、自主代理和对话伙伴继续进入主流，负责评估它们的团队不再问：模型是否给出了正确的答案？

他们越来越多地询问该系统是否足够吸引人，是否为用户创造了足够的价值，以便他们明天、下周或下个月再次回来。

这一转变从根本上改变了评估的含义。

Kaon AI 联合创始人兼首席运营官。

在人工智能时代，“好”是一个不断变化的目标。 令一个用户满意的东西可能会让另一个用户感到沮丧，而为一个企业提供价值的东西可能会被另一个企业认为无关紧要。

这就是为什么成功不能再仅仅通过通用的外部基准、遥测仪表板或“LLM-as-a-judge”分数来衡量。

实时信号

如今，模型变得更加强大，不是通过遵守外部标准，而是基于来自组织内部的跟踪和实时信号。 事实上，评估正在成为组织如何建立和保护其竞争优势的核心部分。

公司越来越多地在内部创建私人评估系统，使用真实的工作流程、机构知识和积累的判断作为标准，根据对其业务重要的结果来衡量进展情况。

订阅 TechRadar Pro 时事通讯，获取您的企业成功所需的所有热门新闻、观点、功能和指导！

新目标不仅仅是评估模型性能，而是创建一个学习循环，在这个循环中，人类的专业知识不断改进人工智能系统，而人工智能系统反过来又会增强人类的专业知识。

这种反馈循环将组织知识转变为复合资产。 每次互动都会产生新的培训信号，加强机构记忆并提高未来绩效。

在这个新世界中，私人评估是企业建立、保留和复合其独特智力资本的机制。

工具不再适合用途

在代理系统中，体验的质量是通过长序列的交互而不是单独的输出来体现的。

许多评估基准仍然严重依赖轮次分析，根据预定义的标准测量孤立的提示响应对。 这些可以在理论上识别模型的功能——幻觉、毒性或语法错误——但它们无法可靠地确定是否是遗忘的偏好、断裂的记忆链或用户体验的微妙退化导致用户在几天或几周后脱离。

随着消费者人工智能的日益普及，偏好学习越来越多地在整个用户旅程中运行，而不是在孤立的提示内运行。 仪表板可以对个人响应进行评分，但它无法完全理解为什么用户三天后返回、在会话中途放弃工作流程或学会完全信任一种交互而不是另一种交互。

这些信号通常存在于产品本身内部。

AI重新定义评测：第一方上台

这就是为什么评估正在从旁观的支持功能转变为核心产品功能。

开发团队越来越多地摆脱外部仪表板和通用评分系统，并将专有的反馈循环直接构建到他们的产品中。 这些系统结合了行为分析、用户保留数据、偏好学习、强化信号和针对自己的应用程序定制的训练后管道。

他们的理由很简单：靠近用户是理解“好”真正含义的唯一方法。

有望获胜的人工智能公司是那些构建连接用户行为、离线分析、奖励模型重新校准和在线验证的闭环系统的公司。 最先进的人工智能产品已经使用实时行为反馈来完善响应、个性化交互并提高保留率。

静态离线基准正在让位于实时偏好学习。 孤立的单轮测试正在被轨迹级行为分析所取代。 评估正在从AI产品的支撑层转向核心操作系统。

传统评估厂商的命运

那么，随着人工智能提供商吸收更多堆栈，LangSmith、Arize 和 Weights & Biases 等知名平台将何去何从？

有趣的是，这些公司面临的最大威胁可能不是来自 Anthropic 或 OpenAI，而是来自他们自己的客户。

这些供应商不一定会被上面取代。 随着人工智能公司意识到评估与产品本身密不可分，它们越来越多地被自下而上地绕过和忽视。

通用第三方平台可以确定答案是否类似于基准数据。 外部可观测性供应商可以处理遥测和表面分析。 但它们并没有真正与日益定义产品质量的环境联系起来。

每一家认真的人工智能公司现在都发现了同样的事情：评估就是产品。 公司不能外包他们的产品。

定义成功是新的关键护城河

这种转变正在加速，因为人工智能堆栈的其余部分正变得越来越商品化。

获得高性能基础模型的机会正在迅速扩大。 初创公司和企业都可以以相对较低的进入门槛访问强大的 API。 及时的工程不太可能继续成为持久的差异化因素。 基本编排层正在变得标准化。 甚至通用的“法学硕士作为法官”评分系统也越来越多地作为内置平台功能提供。

随着这些层成为商品，公司对用户成功的内部理解就成为更重要的差异化因素。

对于编码助理来说重要的信号与对于医疗保健代理、辅导系统或人工智能伴侣来说重要的信号不同。 即使在同一类别中，公司也可能会针对完全不同的结果进行优化，包括参与度、信任、效率、情感共鸣或长期保留。

在模型、基础设施和工具越来越多地被租用的世界中，成功的定义是可以而且必须拥有的东西。 事实上，它可能成为公司拥有的最重要的知识产权。
